new_candidates.date_enacted: County Commission approved Ordinance 2026-13 by a 2-0 vote (Commissioner Paul Cozzens absent) on 2026-05-26.
new_candidates.duration: 180 days. Bars acceptance or processing of new applications for data centers, data center power plants, and solar power plants while the county develops updated regulations. Complete applications were exempt (the Pronghorn/Antelope Data Center application was identified as complete and exempt); incomplete pending applications were suspended (the BrightNight Red Butte application was placed on hold).
new_candidates.trigger: Adopted while the county develops updated data center and solar power plant regulations.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-07-31; 180-day pause from 2026-05-26. This is distinct from the Antelope Data Center conditional-use permit the Planning Commission approved on 2026-06-04, which county staff say was deemed complete before the moratorium took effect and so was not blocked by it.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Pronghorn Development LLC's Antelope Data Center application (deemed complete, exempt); BrightNight's Red Butte Energy and Data Center Campus application (incomplete, placed on hold)

evidence.supports: Official commission minutes reproducing the adopted text of Ordinance 2026-13 and recording the 2-0 vote
County project-status page confirming the moratorium's effect on the Red Butte and Antelope applications

new_candidates.notes: A separately linked standalone ordinance PDF on the county site is dated June 8 and has blank signature/voting lines, inconsistent with the official May 26 minutes [VERIFY on that standalone copy], but the official meeting minutes independently confirm passage and text. This is a genuinely enacted county ordinance, not the candidate's-advocacy-event that a prior research pass mistakenly treated as a moratorium (that earlier item was the May 7 Planning Commission public-comment session on the Antelope Data Center, which took no action).

new_candidates.date_enacted: County Commission unanimously adopted Ordinance 654 on 2026-06-10.
new_candidates.duration: 180-day temporary land-use regulation on data centers, data center power plants, and associated digital infrastructure in areas where the county retains land-use authority. Stops new land-use and business-license applications, building permits, administrative appeals, conditional use permits, subdivisions, zone changes, site plans, development agreements, and similar approvals. Applications formally determined complete before the effective date may proceed; incomplete covered applications are suspended.
new_candidates.trigger: Adopted while the county develops updated data center regulations, in areas outside the Military Installation Development Authority's Stratos project area.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-07-31; 180-day pause from 2026-06-10. County officials expressly stated it does not affect the Stratos project, because the Military Installation Development Authority (MIDA), not the county, controls land use within that project area.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Explicitly does not apply to the Stratos project (MIDA-controlled project area)

evidence.supports: Adopted text of Ordinance 654 establishing the 180-day data center moratorium
County announcement of adoption, clarifying the ordinance does not affect Stratos

new_candidates.notes: Separate and distinct from the Stratos project area (MIDA-controlled), which is not affected by this county ordinance.

new_candidates.date_enacted: County Council suspended its rules and voted 6-0 (one member absent) to adopt Ordinance 2026-32 on 2026-06-23.
new_candidates.duration: Proactive 180-day moratorium on data centers and data center power plants across all zones in unincorporated Cache County, pausing covered land-use, license, permit, appeal, conditional-use, subdivision, zone-change, site-plan, development-agreement, and similar applications (applications already determined complete may continue). Directs staff and the Planning Commission to prepare permanent regulations within 150 days.
new_candidates.trigger: Proactive measure; minutes state the county had received no data center inquiries and the action was not a response to a pending project.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-07-31; 180-day pause from 2026-06-23, adopted proactively with no pending data center project.

evidence.supports: Adopted Ordinance 2026-32 text and county release describing scope and 150-day permanent-regulation directive
Official final minutes recording the 6-0 vote

new_candidates.date_enacted: Municipal Council voted 5-0 to adopt Ordinance 26-12 on 2026-06-30, following a public hearing; published and effective 2026-07-01.
new_candidates.duration: 180-day moratorium throughout Logan City: the city may not accept, process, approve, or issue an application, permit, or approval authorizing construction or development of a data center or data center power plant, and no person may begin such development. Expires after 180 days unless the council ends it earlier.
new_candidates.trigger: City departments had begun work on land-development and utility-related proposals; adopted to allow further Planning Commission review and public comment.

evidence.supports: Adopted text of Ordinance 26-12 establishing the 180-day moratorium
Final special-meeting minutes recording the 5-0 vote
Adoption/publication notice confirming the 2026-07-01 effective date
